overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by waiting 11 to 14 months to create executive session minutes, declined to review the release-of-minutes claim, and declined to find the violation intentional.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to create and maintain minutes of five executive sessions held Jan-Apr 2024 until they were reviewed and approved.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to create and maintain executive session minutes capable of being reviewed at reasonable intervals (intervals of three to six months, starting on the meeting date), the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to release executive session minutes from 2024 after the purpose for those sessions had expired.
allegations.key_passage: As the plaintiff does not articulate a basis for this belief, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the violation was intentional; the AG considered whether the Board knowingly violated the law under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board has not previously been advised that the conduct at issue here violated the Open Meeting Law, we decline to find its violation intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements (create and maintain executive session minutes so they can be reviewed at reasonable intervals).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law’s requirements and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
